property_summary: For any caller and any new owner address, after transferOwnership is called, if the new owner is not the current owner, the owner should only update to the new owner if the caller is the current owner; the bug allows any caller to change owner to any new address.

For any caller and any new owner address, after transferOwnership is called by an address that is not the current owner, the owner should remain unchanged; the bug allows a non-owner to change the owner.
For any caller, a transferOwnership call always changes the owner to the new owner; the buggy version allows any non-owner to successfully change it too.
After any call to transferOwnership, the owner state variable must equal the passed newOwner argument; the buggy version ignores the argument so owner remains unchanged, violating this invariant.
After calling transferOwnership, the owner must equal the new owner; the bug never updates it, so an initially-owner caller stays owner instead of the new one.
After a successful transferOwnership, owner must equal the newOwner; the bug never updates owner so the invariant fails.

For any address, calling `owned()` succeeds when executed by the owner and fails when executed by a non-owner in the reference, but the mutated modifier inverts this, causing `owned()` to succeed for non-owners and fail for the owner.

The reference contract C allows the owner to transfer ownership to any address, and after a successful transfer the new owner matches the address passed to transferOwnership; the buggy contract prevents the true owner from transferring and thus changes ownership only when a non-owner calls it (which will revert in the reference), so after any call to transferOwnership by the current owner, the owner stays the same in the buggy version but updates in the reference.
